title: Silicon Valley's AI wunderkind launches Underdog, the most private Instinct/Muse competitor yet
key_facts: Sigil Wen, a Thiel Fellow, launched an invite-only beta of Underdog on Monday
Model runs wholly on-device on Macs and Windows PCs; Linux, iPhone and Android coming
Powered by Husky, inference engine Wen built
Uses a 27-billion-parameter reasoning model fine-tuned from Qwen3.8-27B
Wen says it compares favourably with Claude Opus 4.6 on some benchmarks
Free at first, never ad-supported; takes a tiny percentage of payments made via Stripe
Startup is Conway Research, backed by Andreessen Horowitz, Khosla Ventures and Stripe co-founder Patrick Collison among others
quote_evidence: The model runs wholly on-device, meaning the user’s data remains on devices they already own, currently Macs and Windows PCs, with Linux, iPhone, and Android versions coming soon.
Underdog is, however, using much smaller models than today’s state-of-the-art ones hosted in data centers.
The app will be free at first and never ad-supported.
why_it_matters_hint: An on-device assistant trades model size for privacy, funded by payment fees instead of ads.
notes: Launch was on Monday 5 Oct 2026 per TechCrunch, so one day before the 6 Oct window: score lowered by 1 (6 to 5).
